ALPENGLOW ON THE SUMMIT: the highest point alone ignites in deep rose while every slope below rests in cold blue shadow, burning for one fierce minute
ALPENGLOW ON THE EASTERN RIM: a single rim flares amber-pink, holding that colour while the whole basin beneath waits in pre-dawn violet stillness
FIRST SUN ON THE SPIRE: one narrow spire catches the earliest gold, glowing like an ember above slopes still wrapped in grey-blue shadow
ALPENGLOW ON THE NORTH FACE: the uppermost face flushes salmon then crimson, one concentrated blaze above a world still locked in shadow
FIRST LIGHT ON THE PEAK: a single summit burns brilliant copper for two minutes while every ridge and hollow around it holds the dark
STORM BREAK: one broad soft wide shaft of hazy light punches through torn overcast and lays a sharp, bright pool across the valley floor far below
STORM BREAK SINGLE: a single soft shaft of hazy light slants through the gap and strikes the hillside, isolating one luminous patch in surrounding grey
STORM BREAK SHAFT: a wide soft wide shaft of hazy light forces through a ragged opening and floods one corner of the basin with sudden warm gold
STORM BREAK OVER THE PLAIN: a single soft wide shaft of hazy light reaches the ground and spreads into a glowing oval, everything beyond it still absorbed in storm shadow
CREPUSCULAR FANS THROUGH THE GAP: three broad rays fan outward through a ridge notch, each soft wide shaft of hazy light distinct, edged in pale gold against the haze
HAZY FANS OF LIGHT AT THE PASS: soft hazy fans of light spread wide from a low gap, banding the air with alternating gold and lavender in long diagonal sweeps
CREPUSCULAR LIGHT THROUGH THE COL: soft wide shaft of hazy light pour through the col and splay across the foreground, each shaft softly defined, widening as it reaches lower ground
CREPUSCULAR SPILL FROM THE RIDGE: five rays fan from behind the ridge crest, each soft wide shaft of hazy light tapering toward the camera in a spreading wash of amber light
BACKLIT RIM WITH SUNSTAR: the sun sits at the very edge of the rim, erupting into a tight six-pointed star, the rim itself a dark silhouette rimmed in fire
BACKLIT RIDGE GLOW: light blazes behind the ridge crest, pressing a thin burning line along the top while the face below dissolves into rich shadow
SUNSTAR AT THE HORIZON: the sun drops to the landform edge and flares into a sharp starburst, sending thin spikes of light radiating across the frame
BACKLIT MESA EDGE: the low sun presses behind the flat top, haloing the entire upper edge in blinding gold, the face beneath in deep shade
MOONRISE OVER SNOWFIELD: the full moon clears the ridge and lays a wide silver road across the snowfield, blue-white and sharp-edged in the cold air
MOONLIGHT ON STILL WATER: the moon hangs its reflection as a long soft streak of white light laid across the water surface, trembling only at the far edge
MOONRISE COLOUR ON SNOW: the rising moon washes the upper snowfield in warm ivory, the colour deepening to gold near the horizon before fading upslope
SUNSET WASH ON THE CLIFFS: the last warm light climbs the cliff face, turning the stone from amber at the base to deep red near the rim
COLOUR WASH ASCENDING THE WALL: sunset colour sweeps upward across the vertical face, the band of orange rising visibly as the sun descends below the horizon
SUNSET BLUSH CLIMBING THE ESCARPMENT: a flush of rose and apricot creeps up the escarpment, the colour intensifying as it nears the top edge
LIGHTNING FORK IN THE DISTANCE: one clean white fork reaches the far ground, briefly flooding the entire landscape in a flat, cold, blue-white flash
DISTANT LIGHTNING STRIKE: a single bright fork splits the far sky and touches the earth, illuminating the whole scene for one sharp, silent instant
